text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- SANTOS SLOWS DOWN; OTHER PORTS MODERNIZE
Four years after the approval of a ports law, and while other ports privatize and modernize, Latin America's largest port still faces problems as a result of old-style labor relations.
-- GOVERNMENT TO AID THE CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRY

Pressured by a trade deficit that may top $10 billion this year, the Brazilian government mulls introducing incentives to the capital goods sector in a bid to reduce imports of used machinery and other items.
-- CANADIANS WANT TO INVEST IN BRAZIL
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso arrived Monday in Ottawa for a three-day visit to promote business opportunities in Brazil.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- INDIAN DIES BURNED IN BRASILIA
A Brazilian indian soaked in a flammable liquid and set on fire by five youths over the weekend died Monday in Brasilia of severe burns on 95 percent of his body.
-- END OF CIVIL SERVANT STABILITY WILL AFFECT POOR STATES
If approved by Congress, the end of job stability for civil servants may have a strong impact on the labor market in the north and northeastern states.
O GLOBO
-- LANDLESS MOVEMENT TO INVADE LANDS IN THE NORTHEAST
The Landless Movement (MST) told members Monday to speed up land invasions in Brazil's northeastern states of Pernambuco, Bahia, Maranhao, Ceara and Rio Grande do Norte.
-- SHARK ATTACKS YOUTH IN BUZIOS
Brazilian student Joao Pedro Portinari Leao, 22, was attacked Sunday by a shark while windsurfing in Buzios, Rio de Janeiro state.
- - - -- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
